annotation_description: Choosing to be on the play with this hand is debatable. The hand has no turn-1 play (Breeding Pool could come in untapped but there's nothing to cast for 1 mana with the available colors), and the curve starts at 3 with Formidable Speaker. Being on the draw would give an extra card, which helps find early action and land drops for this slow hand with expensive spells (Deceit at 6, Overlord at 5, Wistfulness at 5). However, being on the play is conventionally correct in most Standard formats to maintain tempo advantage, and this hand does have a reasonable curve into turn 3 Formidable Speaker into turn 4-5 threats. The decision is defensible but worth noting given the hand composition.
human_notes: it is always correct to be on the play.

annotation_description: Playing Cavern of Souls on turn 2 is suboptimal when the hand contains South Pole Voyager (1W) and Earthen Ally (G) that want colored mana. Cavern of Souls only produces colored mana for one chosen creature type. Floodfarm Verge would provide both W and U (with a Plains/Island condition that could be met later), but more importantly, Starting Town enters untapped on turns 1-3 and produces any color of mana for 1 life. Playing Starting Town now guarantees the ability to cast South Pole Voyager (needing W) on turn 2 alongside Floodfarm Verge or another land on turn 3. With Cavern of Souls, the player can only get colored mana for one creature type (likely Ally), which helps cast Ally creatures but is more restrictive. Starting Town is strictly better here since it enters untapped (turn 2) and produces any color, giving maximum flexibility for the diverse mana requirements in hand (W for Voyager, G for Earthen Ally, B for Boiling Rock Rioter).

annotation_description: Playing Earthen Ally (a creature) before combat when the player has Allies at Last (a combat trick) in hand is suboptimal sequencing. However, the more pressing issue is land sequencing: the player has Cavern of Souls as their only land and multiple lands in hand (Floodfarm Verge, Starting Town, Breeding Pool, Starting Town). They should play a land first to have mana available for future turns. Playing Earthen Ally for G requires a green source - Cavern of Souls can produce colored mana only for the chosen creature type, so if Ally was chosen, this works. But the player should play a land drop first (this is their main phase, and they need to make a land drop). They're casting Earthen Ally using Cavern of Souls, but they're skipping their land drop for the turn. They should play a land first (like Breeding Pool untapped paying 2 life, or Starting Town) and then cast Earthen Ally.

annotation_description: Evoking Wistfulness for card filtering (draw 2, discard 1) uses the entire turn's mana when stronger development plays were available. Playing Gloomlake Verge first would give 3 lands, enabling Overlord of the Balemurk for impending cost {1}{B} which starts a powerful threat ticking down, or Formidable Speaker {2}{G} which provides a body and creature tutor.

Discarding Bringer of the Last Gift to Wistfulness's draw-discard trigger. Bringer is a powerful reanimation target that returns all creatures from graveyards when cast, and with Overlord of the Balemurk's mill/reanimate ability available, having Bringer in the graveyard could be useful. However, the player has two Overlord of the Balemurk in hand which can mill and return creatures, so putting Bringer in the graveyard could actually be part of a plan to reanimate it later. The alternative consideration is discarding one of the duplicate Formidable Speakers or duplicate Gloomlake Verges, which are less impactful cards. Discarding a land (Gloomlake Verge) when you only have 2 lands in play and need to ramp to cast expensive threats like Overlord or Ardyn seems wrong. Discarding a duplicate Formidable Speaker might preserve more options since Bringer of the Last Gift is a unique and powerful effect. That said, Bringer costs 8 mana and is very far from being castable, and Overlord can potentially return it from the graveyard, so this discard has some logic to it.

With 4 lands available (producing G, U, B), the player could have cast both Formidable Speaker (2G = 3 mana) and Overlord of the Balemurk for its Impending cost (1B = 2 mana). Wait - that's 5 mana total with only 4 lands. However, Formidable Speaker costs 2G (3 mana) and uses most of the mana, leaving only 1 mana. Overlord impending costs 1B (2 mana). So actually they can't cast both. The real question is whether Formidable Speaker (getting a body + creature tutor) would have been better than Overlord impending. Formidable Speaker tutors a key creature while providing a 2/4 body, which is likely more impactful at this stage.

annotation_description: With only 4 lands producing at most GGUB (Breeding Pool, Hedge Maze, 2x Gloomlake Verge), casting Overlord of the Balemurk for its full cost of {3}{B}{B} requires all 4 lands and is tight on mana. The 5-turn clock to become a creature is acceptable since the opponent has minimal board presence (just lands). By paying full cost, Hype taps out completely, leaving no mana for Spell Snare and gaining only the immediate 5/5 body — which isn't under pressure to need. The Impending cost would have been far more efficient, preserving interaction.

Cast Overlord of the Balemurk for Impending instead of Formidable Speaker. The Overlord won't be a creature for 5 turns, while Formidable Speaker provides an immediate 2/4 body, a creature tutor (discard to search), and leaves 1 mana open for Spell Snare against opponent's 2-drops. With only 4 lands and needing to ramp toward expensive threats like Ardyn or Bringer, the tutor is more impactful than milling 4.

GPT5n Undrdog played Great Divide Guide (a creature) before combat rather than playing a land first. They have multiple untapped lands in hand (Floodfarm Verge, Breeding Pool, Starting Town) and only 2 lands on board. Playing a land first would increase available mana and ensure the land drop isn't missed (they ended up discarding to hand size, suggesting they had more cards than needed). Additionally, casting a creature before combat when holding Allies at Last (a combat trick) is slightly suboptimal sequencing — playing the creature pre-combat telegraphs information. More importantly, with only 2 lands on the battlefield, they should have played a land first to have 3 mana available, which would allow casting Great Divide Guide more efficiently or keeping mana open for other plays.

With 4 lands on board and the postcombat main phase, Grk41F Hype should cast Overlord of the Balemurk for its impending cost of {1}{B} (2 mana) rather than just playing a tapped land. The Overlord's impending mode starts the countdown and triggers mill 4 + recursion on entry, which would retrieve a powerful creature like Bringer of the Last Gift, Wistfulness, or Deceit from the graveyard. Playing Underground Mortuary tapped means no mana was used this turn. They could have played the land AND cast Overlord for impending cost, or at minimum cast the Overlord with available mana. However, looking more carefully: they have Breeding Pool (G/U), Hedge Maze (tapped - entered this turn? No, it entered turn 3), Gloomlake Verge x2 (U, or B if controlling Island/Swamp). Breeding Pool is an Island, so Gloomlake Verge can tap for B. They have access to at least 1B from Gloomlake Verge + Gloomlake Verge, which is exactly {1}{B} for Overlord's impending cost. They could also cast Formidable Speaker for {2}{G} using Breeding Pool for G + two other lands. Playing just a tapped land and passing with 4 mana available wastes the turn.

annotation_description: Casting Overlord of the Balemurk for full cost {3}{B}{B} uses all 5 mana this turn to get an immediate 5/5 with ETB mill 4 + recursion. However, casting it for Impending {1}{B} would only cost 2 mana, leaving 3 mana open - critically leaving up mana for Spell Snare (which costs {U}) to protect against opponent's 2-mana plays. The opponent is at only 2 lands and likely deploying cheap threats. While getting an immediate 5/5 body with ETB is powerful, especially against an opponent with an empty board, the Impending cost would let Grk41F hold up Spell Snare and still develop the Overlord (arriving as a creature in 5 turns). Additionally, with Bringer of the Last Gift in the graveyard, the Overlord's ETB mill could find more creatures but the recursion target (Bringer) is already known. The immediate pressure of a 5/5 against an opponent with no board is strong, but leaving up interaction while still developing is arguably better tempo since the opponent can't block anyway and won't be under lethal pressure immediately.

Discarding Spell Snare removes the only piece of interaction/countermagic from hand. With the opponent at 20 life and only 2 lands in play, they're likely to start deploying 2-mana threats soon (the format where Spell Snare shines). Meanwhile, the hand contains duplicate Overlord of the Balemurk - discarding one of those would preserve interaction while still being castable later or set up graveyard synergies. However, Spell Snare is narrow and the opponent may not have key 2-mana targets, and the Formidable Speaker search is very powerful, so this is debatable rather than a clear mistake.

message: You may choose an alternative cost
annotation_description: With 5 lands available (Breeding Pool, Hedge Maze, Gloomlake Verge x2, Underground Mortuary) and Formidable Speaker already on board, casting Overlord of the Balemurk for full cost {3}{B}{B} uses all 5 mana this turn. The ETB mills 4 and returns a creature/planeswalker from graveyard (likely Bringer of the Last Gift or Deceit). However, casting for impending {1}{B} would only cost 2 mana, leaving 3 mana open for other plays - potentially casting a second Formidable Speaker (2G) this turn for additional value (tutor effect + board presence). The Overlord as a 5/5 creature is nice but the opponent has no board presence (just 2 lands), so there's no urgency for an immediate 5/5 body. The impending version still provides the enchantment's mill/recursion trigger every end step when time counters are removed, and the ETB trigger fires when it enters (even as impending). Actually, wait - with impending, it enters as a non-creature enchantment and the ETB 'whenever this permanent enters' trigger still fires, giving the mill 4 + recursion immediately. So impending gives you the same ETB value while saving 3 mana. The tradeoff is waiting 5 turns for the creature body, but with no opposing pressure at 18 life, that's very manageable. Casting for full cost when you could get the same ETB and have 3 mana for Formidable Speaker's tutor is likely suboptimal.

Returning Bringer of the Last Gift (8 mana) when the opponent is severely mana-screwed at 2 lands. Bringer's symmetrical sacrifice-and-return effect would give back the opponent's graveyard creatures (South Pole Voyager, Earthen Ally). With Grk41F already ahead on board with Formidable Speaker and Overlord, Deceit would be castable sooner and could strip a key card from the mana-screwed opponent's hand, pressing the advantage more efficiently.

With only 2 lands on turn 7 and severe mana screw, Great Divide Guide is one of the most valuable cards in hand since it provides mana fixing/acceleration for all lands and allies. Allies at Last is a situational combat trick requiring multiple allies on board and an opponent's creature - essentially a dead card given the current desperate board state.

Chose to return Harvester of Misery from graveyard to hand when already holding a copy of Harvester of Misery. Deceit would have provided more flexible interaction (bounce a permanent or strip opponent's hand) as a unique option, while the second Harvester is redundant. Additionally, Harvester's -2/-2 ETB would hurt Hype's own Formidable Speaker.

message: Select a creature an opponent controls
annotation_description: Allies at Last allows up to two creatures to each deal damage equal to their power to a target opponent's creature. GPT5n Undrdog chose to target Formidable Speaker (a 2/4) instead of a much more threatening creature. Overlord of the Balemurk is a 5/5 that mills and recurs creatures from the graveyard - it's the primary engine generating card advantage and board presence. Harvester of Misery is a 5/4 with menace that gave -2/-2 on ETB. At 5 life, removing the biggest threat is critical. Without knowing exactly which creatures GPT5n controlled to deal damage, targeting the 2/4 Formidable Speaker over the 5/5 Overlord or 5/4 Harvester wastes the removal spell on the least threatening creature on the opponent's board.

Grk41F Hype has Overlord of the Balemurk (5/5), Harvester of Misery (5/4), and Formidable Speaker (2/4) on the battlefield against an opponent at 5 life with no creatures. Any combination of attackers totaling 5+ power would be lethal. Overlord alone (5 power) is lethal. Harvester alone (5 power) is lethal. Yet the combat phase passed without declaring any attackers, allowing the opponent to survive at 5 life and take another turn.
